clue.text: Journalists, two by two, taken to political community

parts.note: two multiplied by two makes four
a nation organised under a government is the state

explanation.surface: Reporters are paired up and introduced to the world of politics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Two by two' looks like marching in pairs, but it is a sum: two times two.
explanation.definitionFit: The press is traditionally called the fourth estate, after the clergy, nobility and commons.

clue.text: Chemical symbols representing a double sulphate written up

parts.note: to stand for someone is to represent them

indicators.note: in a down clue, writing upwards means the word is read from the bottom, so backwards

parts.note: alum is a double sulphate of aluminium and potassium

explanation.surface: Notation for a chemical compound is being recorded in a lab notebook.
explanation.walkthrough: Alum is used in dyeing and tanning; 'written up' suits a down clue, where writing upwards reads backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A chemical formula is the string of element symbols showing a compound's make-up.

clue.text: Rank held by clapped-out territorial

indicators.note: the letters are contained within the run of the following words

explanation.surface: A worn-out part-time soldier is kept in his military rank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rank' looks like a military grade but is the adjective, as in 'rank amateur'. Territorial is a member of Britain's part-time Territorial Army.
explanation.definitionFit: Rank and utter both mean complete or absolute, as in 'a rank outsider'.

clue.text: Give someone a ring, then elope frantically

indicators.note: acting frantically suggests wild disorder, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A couple make one call and then run off in a hurry to marry.
explanation.definitionFit: To ring someone in British usage is to call them on the phone.

clue.text: We peel Jaffa, soon ending up with zest

indicators.note: the ending of each of the four words is taken

explanation.surface: Peeling an orange soon leaves us with zest on our hands.
explanation.walkthrough: A Jaffa is an orange; 'zest' pretends to be the peel but is the sense of gusto.
explanation.definitionFit: Elan is dash and vigour, a synonym of zest.

clue.text: Cuppa they say all are refusing to drink

indicators.note: what people say signals a word judged by its sound

parts.note: a cuppa is British slang for a cup of tea
all is the total

explanation.surface: Everyone turns down a cup of tea, apparently.
explanation.definitionFit: A teetotal person abstains from alcohol altogether.

clue.text: Drunk names an unknown to win

parts.note: to tip a horse is to name it as one to win, so names to win gives tips
y is an unknown quantity in algebra

explanation.surface: A drunk gambler picks a dark horse for victory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to win' completes the racing sense of 'names', as in tipping a horse.
explanation.definitionFit: Tipsy means slightly intoxicated.

clue.text: Young OHara about to enter artillery unit (not imperial)

indicators.note: about means going round, so one piece wraps the others

parts.note: Kimball O'Hara is the boy hero of Kipling's novel Kim
to log something is to enter it in a record
RA is the Royal Artillery

explanation.surface: A boy is about to join a gun battery, a metric note added.
explanation.walkthrough: 'artillery unit' reads as one phrase, but 'unit' belongs to the definition; 'about' is the wrapping signal around the boy's name.
explanation.definitionFit: The kilogram is the SI base unit of mass, metric rather than imperial.

clue.text: The world over, knowledge is incomplete

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means the word is flipped upwards, so backwards

parts.note: an orb is a globe, the world
ken is range of knowledge

explanation.surface: Worldwide, human knowledge is admitted to be partial.
explanation.definitionFit: Something broken is not whole or intact.

clue.text: I subsequently returned a note to settle accounts

indicators.note: returned means sent back, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: subsequently means later
te is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: Someone later sent back a message to square things up.
explanation.definitionFit: To retaliate is to pay back an injury, to get even.

clue.text: Superior poet

definitions.meaning: the head of a priory, a monastic superior
Matthew ... was an English poet of the early 1700s

explanation.definitionFit: A prior is a religious superior, and Prior is also the surname of the poet Matthew Prior.

clue.text: Rake introduced to a French female, not yet 21

indicators.note: one piece is put into the other

parts.note: une is the feminine form of a in French
a rip is a rake, a dissolute man

explanation.surface: A womaniser is presented to a young French woman who is under age.
explanation.walkthrough: Twenty-one was the old age of majority in Britain, so 'not yet 21' means immature.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone not yet of age is figuratively green, not fully matured.

clue.text: Fellow and wife entering city's shell in car

parts.note: bod is British slang for a person

indicators.note: one piece goes into the other

parts.note: York is a cathedral city in northern England

explanation.surface: A man and his wife are going into a northern English city.
explanation.definitionFit: The bodywork is the metal outer frame of a vehicle.

clue.text: Start of play concerning lawsuit

parts.note: a play starts with Act I
on means about, concerning

explanation.surface: A theatre opening is the subject of a court case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Start of play' looks like a first-letter pick, but it is the first act.
explanation.definitionFit: A legal action is a case brought in court.

clue.text: Hear about a garment that's a grotesque imitation

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece encloses the rest

parts.note: a judge hears or tries a case
a vest is an undergarment

explanation.surface: Someone listens to talk of a piece of clothing that is a cheap copy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hear' is a judge's verb, as a court hears or tries a case; 'about' is the container signal, not 'concerning'.
explanation.definitionFit: A travesty is a distorted or absurd parody of something.

clue.text: Unbreakable car is not damaged

indicators.note: something damaged is knocked out of shape, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A vehicle that survives unscathed must be indestructible.
explanation.definitionFit: Figuratively cast-iron means solid and impossible to break, as in a cast-iron alibi.

clue.text: Do bathers swim in these east coast waters?

indicators.note: the letters swim around and settle in a new order

explanation.surface: A question whether people go bathing in some eastern English waters.
explanation.walkthrough: The Broads are a network of rivers and lakes in Norfolk and Suffolk on England's east coast.
explanation.definitionFit: The Broads are a famous stretch of inland waterways near the east coast of England.

clue.text: Started and finished as parvenu

definitions.note: used as an adjective here, describing someone newly risen

parts.note: to start in surprise is to jump
up means over, finished, as in time is up

explanation.surface: Someone who began and ended a career as an upstart.
explanation.definitionFit: Jumped-up describes someone who has risen above their station and shows off, a social climber.

clue.text: Watch showing seconds and date

parts.note: to take someone out is to date them

explanation.surface: A timepiece displays the seconds and the calendar date.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Watch' looks like a timepiece but is surveillance.
explanation.definitionFit: A stakeout is a period of covert surveillance.

clue.text: Crush country's spirit

definitions.meaning: to quash or stamp out, as one does a rumour

explanation.definitionFit: To scotch is to put an end to something, and Scotch is the whisky of Scotland.

clue.text: Solitary island has appeal

definitions.note: a noun here, a person who lives alone

parts.note: Herm is one of the Channel Islands
it is slang for sex appeal

explanation.surface: A lonely island nonetheless has its charms.
explanation.definitionFit: A hermit is a recluse who lives apart from others.

clue.text: Went over track and prepared for race

explanation.definitionFit: To train is both to travel by railway and to coach or practise for a contest.

clue.text: I reprove converts past their prime.

indicators.note: converts means changes form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone scolds new believers who are getting on in years.
explanation.walkthrough: 'converts' looks like a noun for new believers but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Overripe fruit has gone beyond its best, figuratively past one's peak.

clue.text: In scripture lessons, psalm is missing last verse

indicators.note: one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: RE is religious education, a school subject in Britain
a psalm is a sacred song, a hymn

explanation.surface: A Bible lesson's psalm lacks its final stanza.
explanation.walkthrough: 'last' belongs with 'is missing', not with 'verse'; 'In' is the container signal for the school subject.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhyme is verse, poetry with matching sounds.

clue.text: Something to be regretted by a part of the Soviet Union

parts.note: a crime is a deplorable act

explanation.surface: An unfortunate deed is done by one Soviet region.
explanation.definitionFit: Crimea, the Black Sea peninsula, was part of the USSR when this was set.

clue.text: State with ocean to east

parts.note: the main is an old word for the high sea

explanation.surface: A coastal state lies with the Atlantic on its eastern side.
explanation.definitionFit: Maine is a US state in New England.

clue.text: Sign showing old people

parts.note: men means people

explanation.surface: Elderly folk display a symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: An omen is a portent or sign of the future.

clue.text: Like Siamese or Chinese weight

definitions.meaning: resembling a cat such as the Siamese
a Chinese and Southeast Asian unit of weight

explanation.definitionFit: Catty means cat-like, and a catty is also an Asian unit of weight of about 600 grams.

clue.text: Current stoppage has people cursing

parts.note: a dam stops the flow of a current of water
a nation is a people

explanation.surface: A power cut sets everyone swearing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Current' suggests electricity but is a water flow.
explanation.definitionFit: Damnation is used as a curse, an oath of condemnation.

clue.text: Stay calm -he needs a poke to get excited

indicators.note: getting worked up and agitated, so the letters are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone told to keep cool needs a jab to rouse him.
explanation.definitionFit: To keep one's head is an idiom meaning to remain composed in a crisis.
